title: Contract inclusion and inheritance are implemented against fixture crates only; no real crate publishes, includes or inherits
why: Card CONTRACT-INHERIT added `#include "crate:module";` and `contract inherit [NS::]NAME;` with a published load path (ContractLoadPath: crate name, recorded namespace, version, declared dependencies, owned modules, published subset), a resource-v1 loader over it (load_published_resource_contracts), provenance in ResourceContracts.inclusion_evidence and package include pins in providers/package.py, all exercised against fixture crates under crates/qcore-contract/tests/fixtures/contract_inherit/. Nothing real is wired: (1) the five contract crates (quirin-provider-libc, -cfl, -mpack, -msgpack, -fluent-bit) and quirin-provider-shared record no NAMESPACE or PUBLISHED list beside CONTRACTS and declare no contract-use dependency edges; (2) core crates cannot link provider crates (compiler/tests/workspace_layering.rs), so a real ContractLoadPath needs a generated, digest-pinned load-path manifest (crate, version from Cargo metadata, dependencies, published modules with SHA-256) that a core consumer reads as data; (3) the resource manifest (cycle19-resource-contracts.json, schema 1, file paths) cannot select a `crate:module` reference, so a schema-2 selection is needed before the audit can load an inherited contract, and the audit's contract_inclusion assumptions key is therefore unreachable today; (4) providers/package.py build does not yet write the inventory's `includes` pins or install includes/<crate>/<module>, and the Rust ContractBundle inventory (deny_unknown_fields) refuses an `includes` field; (5) the five qcore-provider-* artifact crates are refused on a load path by the quirin-provider- prefix rule (QI017), so their provider-owned contracts cannot publish or include until they are renamed or the rule is widened by decision; (6) no real contract uses the forms (candidate: wrappers that restate libc contracts, e.g. flb_free/flb_malloc-shaped declarations). Discharge: wire (1)-(4), decide (5), adopt in at least one real module, and show by a corpus arbiter run that the adopted environment's diagnostics equal the hand-written baseline's, with the inheritance chains present in the published assumptions.

title: Clauses after `contract inherit PARENT` are refused (QI002); no sound per-consumer extension rule exists yet
why: Card CONTRACT-INHERIT refuses `contract inherit P { … };`. Whether an added clause is sound depends on the consumer and the clause family: in resource v1 a `requires resource_literal_argument(p, LITERAL);` premise only withdraws call sites and would be a sound strengthening, while an added `ensures normal resource_*` mode duplicates a parameter's mode, which v1 refuses and for which v1 has no strength order at all. A sound admission rule therefore has to be stated per consumer and per clause family, with a Lean theorem that every admitted extension only strengthens (never weakens) the inherited obligations, and a v1 loader check that the extended child's loaded record differs from the parent's only in the admitted direction. Discharge: specify and prove that rule for resource v1 premises (at least), implement it with negative controls for every non-admitted family, or record a decision that extensions stay refused.

title: Only the resource-v1 loader consumes inherited contracts; observation, lifecycle and source-bound interpreters refuse them
why: Card CONTRACT-INHERIT's elaboration (elaborate_contract_module) is interpreter-independent and proves (Lean rename_preserves_meaning) that the positional renaming preserves meaning for any reading that resolves clause words by parameter lookup, but a consumer that reads some positions structurally can diverge (Lean positional_reading_can_diverge), so each consumer must compare its own reading of child and parent before trusting an inherited contract. Only the resource-v1 loader has that comparison. contract_observation, chunk_contract, the lifecycle and source-bound adapters and the frontend's contract envelope all receive unresolved inclusion as a Q000 parse refusal (fail-closed), which is correct but means an observation or lifecycle policy cannot be inherited. Discharge: for each consumer that should accept inherited contracts, add its reading-equality gate over elaborated text with negative controls, or record that it stays refusing.
